chapter: Teaching, the 1951 Big Show and New York nights
title: How Collins teaches: playing tunes in many ways
summary: He plays standards like How High the Moon many different ways so students absorb voicings by listening, and is compiling a book of tunes and original pieces.

story.theme_name: Teaching jazz: schools, students and advice to the young
story.community_name: Becoming a teacher: jazz in schools and conservatories

blocks.x: Chord progressions. This is -- I think this is a gift.
Like you were saying when you were very young you were sitting in a church --
-- and (inaudible) you heard things that you wanted to do, the counterpoint--

Well, you see, these things you can study and get the formal training, but if you don't have a feeling about these things it does no good. So the only way you can -- this is how I teach. I play for my students, and I take solos, any tune that they will like. Maybe they like 'How High The Moon.' Okay, so we'll play it. And then I will play 'How high the Moon' many different ways, and to show them the directions to take, the voicings to use, and for him to listen. Now, this is how you cultivate a feeling for this, you listen, you know, you teach them how to hear the right things and the direction to take.

But now you can't write this in books, you know, you just can't do this. It's not possible. You just have to listen and cultivate a feeling for it. And this is the way you come about this. So this is what I'm doing now, I'm just taking tunes and I'm compiling just a book of tunes. And I'll put a few compositions in there, original compositions in there. And very interesting, you know, they're interesting. And I have my students to play them, and to listen. Because you know, when I play the clubs here with my group most of my audience are my students, all the front row is always my students, you know. Which is good because it kind of motivates me because I'm really playing for them, you know, I'm playing -- I'm saying, see, you know, this is what I taught you today, see, this is the way this should go. Or we do this.
So this is -- I enjoy this, you know.
